question: Does the Dumoloc Small Reservoir Irrigation Project EIS provide dated, site-bounded freshwater fish evidence for Dumuloc River, and are its names, coordinates, and reuse terms suitable for public projection?

method.summary: Reviewed the official EMB-hosted EIS's indexed full text for the project fact sheet, freshwater field methods, sampling-station table, fish table, figure captions, narrative fish discussion, table of contents, and official EMB project listing. The indexed PDF text was searchable and opened for line-level review, but a direct PDF download was blocked by the host's Azure WAF; the table and coordinate layout could not be visually checked. No PDF, table image, figure, or fish photo was retained.
method.proponentAndPreparer: National Irrigation Administration Region I – Pangasinan Irrigation Management Office; EIS prepared by Lichel Technologies, Inc.
method.reuseFinding: No item-specific Creative Commons or other reuse license was identified in the reviewed EIS or linked EMB portal listing. Public access on the official portal is not treated as permission to redistribute the report's tables or fish photographs. Keep only an attributed research summary; publication approval remains false.

study.surveyWaterbodyAsReported: Dumuloc River, at locations described relative to the proposed reservoir dam and existing Dumuloc irrigation system. The proposed reservoir is not treated as an already surveyed lake or reservoir.
study.fieldCampaignDatesAsReported: 30 April–1 May 2019, described as toward the end of the summer season.
study.fishSamplingScope: The EIS says fish and macro-invertebrate sampling was conducted only at Sites 1 and 2 because a local fisherman was available there. These are described as Site 1, Dumuloc River upstream (US), and Site 2, Dumuloc River downstream (DS). Other sites were visited or observed, but are not fish-sampled sites in this account.
study.fishSamplingMethodAsReported: Electro-fishing was used at Sites 1 and 2 to collect fish and other macro-biota. Samples were preliminarily sorted, preserved in ice, and identified in a laboratory. No voucher or accession identifiers were located in the reviewed sections.
study.fishTableHeadingAsReported: Table 2-56: Collected Species of Fishes on the assessed Sites

fishTableRowsAsPrinted.remarksAsPrinted: Golden tank goby, biya; native to the Philippines; dominant species in the river; caught for family consumption; IUCN Red List Status = Green; Least Concern (LC)
Sleepy goby, biya; native to the Philippines; caught for family consumption; IUCN Red List Status = Green, Least Concern (LC)
Lizard goby, bunog; endemic to the Philippines; caught for family consumption; IUCN Red List Status = Not Evaluated
North African catfish, paltat; introduced; a preferred fish for table consumption; IUCN Red List Status = Least Concern (LC)
Nile tilapia; introduced; fished for table consumption; IUCN Red List Status = Least Concern (LC)
Buffon's river garfish, half-beak; susuwit; native; edible but not preferred; reported to be more plentiful in Site 3 (existing Dumuloc RIS); IUCN Red List Status = Not Evaluated
phallostethids; due to small size, the species is unknown to locals; known to be endemic in Luzon; this is the first record of it in Dumuloc River; IUCN Red List Status = Not Evaluated

tableCountArithmetic.note: Arithmetic derived from the table's seven source counts; the report's narrative says seven fish species but does not state these calculated totals as a survey-wide abundance estimate.

study.coordinateReview: The EIS says map coordinates were taken with NoteCam and lists coordinates in Table 2-53. The indexed text extraction does not preserve a visually verifiable row alignment and includes an apparent latitude beginning 19 degrees among Bugallon station values. Because the PDF could not be visually inspected and no datum is stated in the reviewed text, no coordinate was accepted, assigned to a fish site, converted, or mapped.
internalConflicts: The table of contents calls the collected-fish list Table 2-55; the body calls the fish table Table 2-56 and the macro-crustacean table Table 2-57.

The table and figure captions print Gulaphallus mirabiles, but the narrative spells the same reported fish Gullaphalus mirabiles. The source also prints Clarias gariepinnus. Preserve the strings; do not infer accepted taxa or specimen identity from a name lookup.

Two table remarks call the IUCN Red List status Green and Least Concern. Green is retained only as a source transcription and is not treated as a verified Red List category or current conservation assessment.

Zenarchopterus buffonis is said to have been reported as more plentiful at Site 3, while the fish-sampling methods limit specimen collection to Sites 1 and 2. The Site 3 statement is not a sampled Site 3 count.

interpretation: The EIS provides a useful historical freshwater survey lead for two sites on Dumuloc River in Bugallon, with seven source-name rows and site-level counts. It is not a complete inventory of the river, watershed, proposed reservoir, or Pangasinan fishes.

The table entries are preserved verbatim for research review. No taxonomic normalization, independent specimen confirmation, current-presence claim, waterbody-wide range, or conservation-status update is made.

The station table's indexed coordinate text cannot currently support fish-site geometry: station alignment needs visual confirmation, one latitude string appears anomalous, and a coordinate datum is not identified. Do not create map points from it.
The report's catch/use and native/introduced remarks are source statements, not validated bait guidance, current catchability, legal status, public access, or safety information.
The EIS baseline is from 2019 and tied to a proposed irrigation project. It does not establish current river conditions, reservoir colonization, present-day fish presence, or present water safety.
No species assertions, occurrence rows, public-app projection, geometry, or reused photographs were added. Article-derived reuse permission remains unverified; Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The official EIS offers source-located historical survey evidence, but reuse terms are unverified, name and table-number conflicts remain, and indexed coordinate layout could not be visually confirmed. Preserve the seven fish rows as research-only leads; do not publish occurrence or map records.

nextAction: Cross-check all seven printed fish names against authoritative taxonomic catalogues while retaining the EIS strings, then seek a visually accessible official copy if station-level geometry is needed. Keep any accepted-name candidate separate from specimen validation and do not promote the counts to current presence or catch advice.
